record.provider: Telnyx Object Storage ($6/TB, zero metered egress)

free_tier.stated: 10 GiB of US storage, 1 million state-change (Class A) and 10 million state-read (Class B) operations free every month; US storage beyond it USD 0.006 per GiB a month; EU storage has no free tier and costs USD 0.025 per GiB a month
free_tier.notes: on the Trial account tier, Cloud Storage is limited to the documented free tier of used capacity, to non-public bucket and object policies or ACLs and to pre-signed URLs with a 5-minute TTL

per_object_cap.stated: 5 TiB per object (a completed multipart upload); 5 GB per single PUT request, 5 GB per part, 10,000 parts at most per multipart upload
per_object_cap.notes: a multipart part is 5 MiB to 5 GB except the final part; a bucket holds at most 50 million objects and an account at most 100 buckets; the limits page says these are subject to change

retention.stated: no expiry is stated while available credit is positive; when available credit stays negative for 30 days the account is abolished and all data is irreversibly purged
retention.notes: the account suspension and loss of data section of the first-party billing documentation

egress.terms: the pay-as-you-go rate card lists Egress fees: None; reads are billed as state-read operations at USD 0.04 per million
egress.price_per_tb: none: the rate card lists no egress fee

record.tooling: AWS SDKs, AWS CLI and third-party S3 clients, authenticated with the Telnyx API key; buckets in us-central-1, us-east-1, us-west-1, eu-central-1, ap-southeast-1 and ca-central-1
record.chaining: S3-compatible origin with no egress fee on the rate card, billed per GiB stored and per million operations

limits.value: 10 GiB of US storage, 1 million state-change and 10 million state-read operations free a month; usage beyond them is billed, and EU storage has no free tier

record.limits_note: minimum billable object size 4 KiB, and metadata counts toward stored bytes; stored bytes are recorded hourly and debited from the account balance; while available credit is negative the free tier is unavailable and new buckets and uploads are refused

identity_cost.detail: reaching the Paid tier needs a verified email, a passed fraud review (LinkedIn or GitHub verification or an AI agent evaluation), a verified mobile number, a payment with a credit or debit card, 2FA and a Provided Service Address; the Trial tier needs only the verified email and the fraud review; the Verified tier adds KYC

record.reliability_note: with a negative available credit, data is retained but API requests fail with UserSuspended until a payment restores the credit; after 30 days of negative credit the account is abolished and all data is irreversibly purged
record.confidence_note: the rate card is quoted from the first-party pricing page, the free tier, regional prices, minimum object size and suspension terms from the first-party billing documentation, and the account tiers from the first-party developer documentation

record.price_per_tb_month: USD 0.006 per GiB a month for US storage beyond the free 10 GiB (about USD 6.14 per TiB), USD 0.025 per GiB a month in the EU (about USD 25.60 per TiB); beyond the free quotas, US operations cost USD 0.50 per million state-change and USD 0.04 per million read requests, EU operations USD 5.00 and USD 0.40 per million; minimum billable object size 4 KiB
record.notes: Unlimited, $0.006 per GiB/month (≈$6.14/TB), no platform fee. Confirmed live: '$0.006per GB/mo', '$0platform fee', and the page's own worked example '10,000 GB STORED … $60.00'.
record.binding_note: the free 10 GiB of US storage a month is the first limit reached; every GiB beyond it is billed at USD 0.006 a month

card.summary: 10 GB of storage free with 1 million state-change operations and 10 million state-read operations

free_tier.stated: 10 GB of storage free with 1 million state-change operations and 10 million state-read operations

egress.terms: Zero egress fees at all volumes: rate card states 'Egress fees None' with unmetered outbound network bandwidth.

record.tooling: the standard S3 API, so rclone s3 and any S3 SDK apply
record.chaining: 10 GB per account with no card needed and no egress charge is 50 accounts for 500 GB, which is absurd for the volume but worth noting for the egress model alone. The paid rate at USD 6.14/TB/month with genuinely free egress is a solid second to the cheapest paid option

limits.value: 10 GB is the free tier total, which is the cap in practice
public buckets appear to require KYC: '开公开桶似乎要KYC认证'

identity_cost.detail: an email address. The forum reports the 10 GB tier needs no card: '免费10G 不用绑卡好像也没流量费'. A public bucket adds a KYC step

record.reliability_note: A telecom company diversifying into object storage, and the zero-egress term is real. The 10 GB cap and the KYC step on public buckets are what close it. The pricing page now frames the product around egress to inference, so the object-storage-only customer is no longer the commercial focus

evidence.proved: 'Storage USD 0.006 per GiB (billed monthly)'; 'Egress fees None'; 'State-change operations USD 0.50 per million'; 'USD 60.00 Per month ... 10,000 GB STORED'. The API path advertised on the page, GET /v2/public/pricing, returns 404

'免费10G 不用绑卡好像也没流量费'

record.price_per_tb_month: USD 6.14/TB/month at USD 0.006/GiB, with no egress charge at any volume
record.binding_note: 10 GB free, so the quota closes it. On the paid tier the egress term is the best of the providers compared, and the storage rate is USD 6.14/TB/month, three times the price floor of paid storage.
record.notes: Evaluates zero-egress file distribution. The free 10 GB promotional tier requires identity verification and card authorization, while standard paid storage is available under published zero-egress rates.
